tasks.short: Teach the class and small groups through explanation, discussion and demonstration, and check who understood.

steps.what: Teacher opens the lesson on the digital board and checks the plan
Teacher instructs students as a class: explains, discusses, demonstrates
Teacher gives extended instruction to a small group at the instruction table
Teacher walks round helping individual students during practice
Teacher checks understanding with an exit question and the practice results screen
Teacher notes who needs extended instruction next lesson in the group plan

tasks.design: Configure the practice platform ({LMS}) to show results per lesson goal right after practice, and add a small query that proposes tomorrow's extended-instruction group from those results for the teacher to adjust. Instruction itself stays the teacher's; the group list replaces the hand-kept spreadsheet.
tasks.previous_blocker: Practice results and group plans sat in different places, so teachers copied them by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice platforms already hold results per goal and can export them; a fixed threshold rule proposes a group.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining, motivating and reading the room are the job; thresholds miss pupils who guess right.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing confusion on a face, changing the explanation on the spot and keeping thirty children engaged.

ambition.what: Extended-instruction groups set from the same day's results for every lesson, not once a week.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; the teacher decides groups from a proposal instead of a blank sheet.

reach.learn: Whether the proposed group list helps assistants prepare.

evidence.claim: Pupil records systems in Dutch primary schools track learning goals per pupil.
Practice platforms can show results per lesson goal right after practice.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes or steers education level is high-risk; a fixed threshold rule proposing a group, decided by the teacher, is not an AI system.
Parents and staff councils must consent to rules on pupil data under the Dutch school participation act.

assumptions: Boundary: from opening the lesson to the next lesson's group list; lesson preparation is outside.
Input contract: practice results per pupil and lesson goal, produced by the practice platform; fallback is the teacher's own check.
The school already uses a practice platform; no new pupil data is collected.
unknowns: Whether the practice platform exports results per goal.
How group plans are kept today.
research_questions: Do pupils proposed by the rule match the teacher's own choice?

already_counted.description: Teacher reviews and adjusts the proposed group.

incremental.description: Teacher corrects lesson-goal tags when the platform and method disagree.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A teacher who already works from the platform's screen saves only the spreadsheet step; most time is instruction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree class rules, correct behaviour during lessons, handle incidents, log them and inform parents.

steps.what: Teacher agrees class rules for behaviour with students and posts them
Teacher reminds, praises and corrects behaviour during lessons
Teacher talks with the students involved in an incident
Teacher logs the incident in free text in the pupil records system
Teacher writes or phones parents about serious or repeated incidents
Internal support coordinator follows up repeated incidents with the teacher

tasks.design: Configure a quick incident form in the pupil records system ({OTHER}) with fixed categories, pupils involved and agreed follow-up, usable from a phone. A template fills a parent message from the record for the teacher to edit and send through the parent app, and a rule notifies the internal support coordinator when a pupil reaches three incidents in a month.
tasks.previous_blocker: Incidents went into free text, so nothing could be counted, and every parent message was written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records systems support custom forms, templates and notifications.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping order is relationship work; categories can feel bureaucratic and parents expect a personal tone.
tasks.human_edge: Calming a conflict, being fair and consistent, and knowing when a child's behaviour signals something at home.

ambition.what: A monthly look at incident patterns per class in the team meeting, so support starts before problems grow.

tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; logging and parent messages take less time.

reach.task: Report incidents seen in the playground
reach.learn: Whether assistants can use the same quick form.

evidence.claim: Dutch pupil records systems hold pupil records and connect to a parent app.
Parents' and staff councils must consent to rules on pupil data and to tools that can monitor staff.
Schools process pupil data under their public task; retention of incident records needs a set period.

assumptions: Boundary: from agreeing rules to parents informed and repeated cases flagged; formal measures such as suspension are outside.
Input contract: incident with date, category, pupils involved, short description and follow-up, produced by the teacher; fallback is free text.
No model writes parent messages; the template only fills facts from the record.
Internal support coordinator time is outside the teacher's savings.
unknowns: Whether the school's records system allows custom incident forms.
The school's agreed retention period for incidents.
research_questions: Do fixed categories make incident patterns visible earlier?

already_counted.description: Teacher reviews and edits the template-filled parent message before sending it.

incremental.description: Teacher picks categories consistently and corrects misfiled incidents.
School leader keeps categories, templates and the flag rule current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A calm class with few incidents gives little logging to save; correcting behaviour in the moment is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Notice students who struggle or show special interests, talk with them, plan support and agree it with parents.

steps.what: Teacher notices a student struggling or showing a special academic interest
Teacher talks one-to-one with the student about the problem or interest
Teacher pulls results, notes and earlier approaches from the pupil records
Teacher consults the internal support coordinator on next steps
Internal support coordinator advises on approach and possible support
Teacher writes the agreed approach as a note in the student's file

loop.input: The teacher's short bullets from the conversation and the consult, plus the student overview.
loop.output: A file note in the school's format: observation, what the student said, agreed approach, review date.
loop.check: Every sentence must trace to a bullet or a field in the overview; a word list blocks diagnostic labels and emotion claims; dates and names must match the record.
loop.stop: Two redrafts at most; then the teacher writes the note. The teacher reads and edits every note before saving.
loop.why_not_simpler: The teacher's bullets are free text in varied order; a fixed template cannot turn them into a readable note.

steps.what: Teacher meets parents to discuss the problem and the agreed approach

tasks.design: A query on the pupil records system ({OTHER}) builds a one-page student overview (results trend, notes, attendance, earlier approaches) before the consult. After it, a bounded model step on the school's governed {DATA_PLATFORM} drafts the file note from the teacher's bullets; the teacher edits and saves it, and nothing is stored without that check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Overviews meant clicking through several screens, and file notes were written from scratch after school.
tasks.enabler_now: Records systems export pupil data for a template, and language models draft short notes from bullets under a processing agreement.
tasks.still_hard: Support needs are sensitive health data; the conversation with the child and parents cannot be shortened.
tasks.human_edge: Earning the child's trust, sensing what is behind a problem and agreeing a plan parents support.

ambition.what: Students with a special interest who get an agreed enrichment plan, not only students who struggle.

tasks.altitude: The teacher spends less after-school time on overviews and notes; decisions on support stay with teacher and coordinator.

reach.learn: Whether file notes in one format make follow-up visible.

evidence.claim: Dutch pupil records systems hold pupil records, support plans and learning-goal tracking.
Support needs in a pupil's plan are health data, and new pupil-data systems need a DPIA.
An education IT cooperative advised against a general office AI assistant in 2024 and still found medium privacy risks in 2025, including wrong personal data.
Inferring pupils' emotions with AI is banned, so the draft step must not label emotions.

assumptions: Boundary: from noticing the student to the approach agreed with parents; formal support plans are outside.

Input contract: results per subject and goal, notes, attendance and earlier approaches, produced by staff in the pupil records system; the teacher's bullets after the consult; fallback is writing the note by hand.
The model runs under the school board's processing agreement; no names go to consumer services.
Internal support coordinator time is outside the teacher's savings.
unknowns: Whether the school board has a governed model service and a DPIA for it.
How many such cases a teacher handles per term.
research_questions: How often do teachers change the drafted note, and in what way?

already_counted.description: Teacher reads and edits every drafted file note.

incremental.description: Teacher writes bullets in the agreed form and reports bad drafts.
School board's IT keeps the template, word list and model service running.

approvals.approved_version: The file note text as edited and saved by the teacher; any later change is a new version.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Teachers who keep short notes already save little on writing, and cases with many records still need reading.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Adapt instruction and materials to students' levels and interests: easier texts, enrichment, visual versions.

steps.what: Teacher reviews practice results and the group plan to see students' needs
Teacher decides the adaptation per group: simpler text, extra steps, enrichment
Teacher searches the method and online sources for suitable materials
Teacher rewrites teaching materials at another level or makes a visual version

loop.input: The source text or worksheet, the target level and the lesson goal chosen by the teacher.
loop.output: A rewritten text or worksheet at the target level with key words and an answer key.
loop.check: A readability score and grade word list confirm the level; every key term and fact of the source appears; the answer key is recomputed against the new text; the teacher reads every version before use.
loop.stop: Two redrafts at most; then the teacher adapts by hand.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rewriting prose at another reading level needs language generation; templates cannot do it.

steps.what: Teacher prints the materials or assigns them per group in the practice platform
Teacher discusses adaptations for students with support needs with the coordinator

tasks.design: Results per lesson goal from the practice platform ({LMS}) show which groups need what; the school's material library in {DOCS} is tagged by goal and level. A bounded model step drafts a text or worksheet at the level the teacher picks, checked for level, key terms and answer key, and the teacher reads and approves each version before assigning it.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rewriting a text at three levels took an evening, so most adaptation was done orally or not at all.
tasks.enabler_now: Lesson editors now rewrite text at another level, and two randomised trials found shorter preparation time with no drop in quality.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing what each child needs is judgement; drafts can be wrong or flat, and teachers in one trial used the tool for few lessons.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what will engage this child and when an easier text helps or holds them back.

ambition.what: Strong readers who get enrichment texts every week, not only pupils who struggle.

tasks.altitude: The teacher decides and reviews rather than rewrites; adaptations happen for more lessons.

reach.task: Prepare materials for a small group
reach.learn: Whether assistants can run the draft step under the teacher's choice of level.

evidence.claim: A Dutch lesson editor rewrites text at another level, summarises and translates.
An adaptive practice platform drafts a class activity for a lesson goal.
A randomised trial with 259 teachers cut weekly planning from 81.5 to 56.2 minutes with a chatbot and guide, with no quality difference.
A randomised trial with 464 primary teachers cut weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours, but the tool covered 7% of lessons and use declined.
A school that adapts an AI tool can become its provider under the AI Act.

assumptions: Boundary: from reviewing needs to adapted materials assigned; teaching the lesson is outside.
Input contract: results per goal from the practice platform; source text chosen by the teacher; target level from the teacher; fallback is adapting by hand.
No pupil names or data go into the draft step; it works on teaching texts only.
The draft step runs on a model service approved by the school board.
unknowns: Whether the school board has approved a model service for staff.
How many adapted versions a teacher makes per week today.
research_questions: Does adaptation for more lessons change pupil results over a term?

already_counted.description: Teacher reviews each drafted version for level, accuracy and fit before approving it.

incremental.description: Teacher tags materials by goal and level and reports poor drafts.
School board's IT keeps the model service, checks and word lists running.

approvals.approved_version: The adapted text or worksheet and answer key as the teacher reviewed it in s4; any edit needs a new review.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: As in the primary-school trial, teachers may use the draft step for a small share of lessons and drop it over time, so saving stays near the trial's lower figures.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher keeps instruction, order and the conversations with children and parents; copying results, writing notes and rewriting texts shrink.
reach: Instructional coordinators' follow-up of agreed approaches
skills_to_grow: Judging and correcting drafted materials quickly
Reading results per lesson goal to set groups
Writing short structured notes the school can follow up
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who adapts most lessons for three levels, sets daily groups from results, and spends the time saved with the children who need it.

job.title: Elementary School Teachers, Except Special Education
